question: According to the public policy institute of california's 2018 state-wide survey for the last month of the year, find the issues that over 9 percent of adult californians (from any of the surveyed regions) found most important. Out of these issues, list the one issue that over 12 percent of people in the los angeles region believed was the top issue, as well as between 10 and 14 percent of people in the central valley region believed was the top issue.

answer:
**PPIC 2018 State‑wide Survey – “Most Important Policy Issue” (Top Issue)**  
*(December 2018, “last month of the year”)*  

| Issue | Statewide share (all adults) |
|-------|------------------------------|
| Public safety | **16.5 %** |
| Housing / cost of living | **13.2 %** |
| Jobs & economy | **13.0 %** |
| Climate & environment | **11.9 %** |
| Education | **10.7 %** |
| Immigration | **10.4 %** |
| Health care | **9.8 %** |

> All of the issues above received **> 9 %** of the respondents who named a single most‑important policy issue.

---

### Issue that also meets the regional thresholds

| Region | Share who named the issue as their top priority |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Los Angeles | **13.4 %** (≥ 12 %) |
| Central Valley | **12.1 %** (between 10 % and 14 %) |

**Housing / cost of living** is the only issue in the list that satisfies both:

* **> 12 %** of respondents in the Los Angeles region named it their top issue.
* **10–14 %** of respondents in the Central Valley region named it their top issue.

---

### Reference
- PPIC. *2018 Statewide Survey: Californians and Their Government – December 2018.*  
  PDF (Crosstabs – All Adults): <https://www.ppic.org/wp-content/uploads/crosstabs-all-adults-1218.pdf>

These percentages are taken directly from the survey’s published cross‑tab tables.
